# NOTES: TINMAN by Tom Gallon (single book, Parts I and II)

## Front matter
- Title: TINMAN. Author: Tom Gallon. Publisher: Small, Maynard & Company, Boston, 1907. Also author of "Jarwick the Prodigal," "Tatterly."
- PART I: Ch I "What I Found in the Wood" (p9); II "And What I Lost" (25); III "Her Wedding Day" (41); IV "The Killing of the Lie" (56); V "Alas! for Poor Prince Charlie!" (72); VI "I Leave the World" (87).
- PART II: I "Mine Enemy" (103); II "Ghosts" (119); III "I Enter Upon Servitude" (136); IV "The Coming of the Wolves" (153); V "I Touch Disaster" (170); VI "Love with the Veiled Face" (187); VII "News of the Prisoner" (203); VIII "I Assist the Enemy" (220); IX "I Know the Way at Last" (237); X "Too Late!" (254); XI "I Tell the Truth" (271); XII "The Haunted Man" (288); XIII "I Face the World Again" (305).

## Narrator and frame
- Narrator: Charles Avaline, "Charlie," later prisoner No. 145, later "Tinman," later goes by "Charlie" again and "Mr. Charles Avaline" in Barbara's end. Writes in old age, in a garret and prison, admitting he killed two men. Opens: "I have lived two lives." Age 20 at the start, about 40 when released.
- Narrator's dead parents; ward of guardian Jervis Fanshawe; wanted to be an artist, painter.

## Principal characters
- **Jervis Fanshawe**: guardian, manager of Patton & Co. in the City, office in a narrow dingy court. About 35 at start, long clean-shaven face, long thin nose with wide nostrils, deep cut in chin, thin white fingers that twine over each other, plucks at lips. Gambler in debt to Gavin Hockley; embezzler of Charles's money. Lives in Bloomsbury (old-fashioned house); later rooms near the river (lodging house, girl Moggs). Loves/hates Barbara Patton (rejected by her). Later testifies against Charles. Sent to prison seven years for forgery and fraud. Later plots with Olivant. Kills Murray Olivant in Lincoln's Inn Fields, then sails on the Eaglet in Olivant's place and dies when it wrecks off Ushant.
- **Gavin Hockley**: big young man, about ten years older than Charles, dark moustache, swaggering, carries a cane, rakish, gambler and bully. Taunts Barbara as "a lady of many loves." Charles strikes him on the temple on the terrace at Hammerstone Market (first); then at his Lincoln's Inn Fields rooms Charles kills him with a sword (second, the murder for which he is convicted). Hockley's rooms are in a curious old house in Lincoln's Inn Fields with a flagged courtyard.
- **Barbara Patton** (first Barbara): about 18 when met, very fair, sings; daughter of Mr. Patton, of Hammerstone Market house. Writes note "Because I love you and trust you..." signed BARBARA; calls Charles "my poor Prince Charlie." Marries Lucas Savell. Believed dead at sea; actually escaped the voyage with help of a stewardess, lived under name "Barbara Avaline," returns in her veil-like disguise to save her daughter. Later reunited with Charles; they marry.
- **Lucas Savell**: good-humoured, tall, pleasant-faced cousin of Barbara; later melancholy drinker, pathetic; struck down by stroke, never speaks again; dies some three months before the wedding.
- **Mr. Patton**: old, white-haired, stooping, benevolent, dictatorial; gives toast announcing Barbara's engagement to Lucas Savell; dies later.
- **Murray Olivant**: rich, bullying, half-brother of Arnold Millard; wears "dark" clothes; long legs; cigar; "a keen blade." Loves new Barbara; takes Barbara with Dawkins. Pretends to sail on Eaglet and hides; killed by Fanshawe with a knife in his breast; buried as unknown in pauper's grave.
- **Arnold Millard**: young painter, good-humoured, dependent on half-brother Olivant; loves new Barbara; vows to kill Olivant. Marries new Barbara at the end.
- **Barbara Savell** (new/second Barbara): daughter of first Barbara and Lucas Savell; looks and sings like her mother; calls Charles "Tinman"; fleeing Olivant's advances; later rescued and marries Arnold.
- **Dawkins**: "smile," perpetual smiling man, Olivant's friend and accomplice; kidnaps Barbara by forged note signed "TINMAN"; demands £500 for her address.
- **Moggs**: street girl (about 15–16) in shabby lodging near the river; tough, cunning; hides Barbara; helps Charles.
- **Doctor**: at Patton's dinner, tells the story of the man who pits two men against each other by spreading lies about a woman.
- **Prison governor**: former soldier, trim moustache, deep-set grey eyes; announces release after twenty years.
- **Judge**: sentences "And may God have mercy on your soul!" Jury: little bald innocent-looking juryman who weeps.
- **Landlord** of the George, Hammerstone Market; waiter; chambermaid (pretty, weeping).
- **Charles's counsel** and prosecuting counsel: unnamed.
- **Manservant of Olivant**: highly respectable, later sent away.
- **Stewardess** (unnamed) who hid Barbara on voyage.
- **Woman in black** on terrace: first Barbara as shadow.
- Mentioned: Mrs. Patton (not named), Patton's elderly sister, doctor's wife, Lucas's cousin.

## Place names
- London: Bloomsbury (Fanshawe's rooms); Holborn; narrow street off Holborn (Charles's studio, skylight); City court (Patton & Co. office); Lincoln's Inn Fields (Hockley's rooms; later Olivant's rooms); Trafalgar Square (meeting spot); Hammerstone Market (small town, George Hotel, High Street, woods, church, Patton house outside town); the river street where Moggs lives; Ushant (wreck).
- Prison: unnamed; cell with ground-glass window, wooden table, stool, Bible; tinsmith's shop; No. 145.
- Olivant's flat: fashionable quarter. Ship: the Eaglet (small vessel to Mediterranean).

## Events in order (Part I)
1. Charles meets Fanshawe at City office; Fanshawe dines Charles and Hockley at Bloomsbury. Hockley and Fanshawe discuss "Hammerstone Market" trip; Fanshawe plans to go Tuesday. Charles dreams of killing Hockley.
2. At Hammerstone Market (George Hotel), Hockley swaggers, ignores Charles. In woods Charles meets Barbara Patton singing; they fall in love; she asks "Do you like him?" (Fanshawe); she says "I'm afraid of him." Charles stumbles over Hockley, who growls. Hockley ruins Charles's canvas with a muddy heel. Charles sees Fanshawe staring into pool.
3. Charles dines at Patton's; Fanshawe tells Charles he intends to marry Barbara (Charles says she won't love him). Dinner: doctor's story of lies. Lucas Savell's engagement to Barbara announced; Charles's wine glass snaps. Hockley, drunk, makes sneering remarks. Barbara goes out on terrace; Hockley drags her; Charles strikes Hockley on temple; Hockley falls down steps. Barbara and Charles exchange farewell at terrace end; she says "I promised a year ago." Fanshawe praises Charles, says "strike him dead." Hockley demands money from Fanshawe ("within twenty-four hours").
4. Charles returns to London; a week later Fanshawe warns about Hockley's rumours about Barbara and Charles. Fanshawe confesses he proposed to Barbara in the woods and she laughed at him. Charles meets Hockley at Fanshawe's dinner; card game; Charles loses about £30 odd (later £70), writes I.O.U.; Hockley taunts "Lucky at cards, unlucky in love."
5. Barbara's wedding day at Hammerstone Market (church, wedding breakfast, Savell's speech). Barbara gives Charles a note: "Because I love you and trust you..." signed BARBARA. Fanshawe takes Charles to a supper; Hockley toasts "the pretty bride"; Charles flings glass; a second card game; Hockley accuses Barbara of "many loves" in secret. Charles seizes Hockley's throat; Hockley says Charles tried to murder him. Fanshawe takes Charles to Patton's house; Charles drinks; then Fanshawe sends Charles away; Fanshawe sends Hockley's address and cheque ("I have sent a cheque to Gavin Hockley...") not actually sent.
6. Charles goes to Lincoln's Inn Fields; kills Hockley with a sword (struck twice) after Hockley swings a poker. Fanshawe meets him on stairs; Charles: "I've killed Gavin Hockley—and his lie."
7. Charles visits Fanshawe; Fanshawe confesses he never sent the cheque, had been bled by Hockley, used Charles as tool; "I always hated you." Charles is arrested in Holborn studio; confesses "I did kill the man." Trial at Old Bailey-style court: Fanshawe testifies; "Guilty"; sentence of death; reprieved to penal servitude for life "on account of my youth."
8. Charles in prison, three days before execution: dream of Barbara in the wood ("I will reach you—God willing—before they kill you!"). Barbara visits in black; they talk; she promises silence. Reprieve.

## Part II (events in order)
1. Charles is in prison twenty years (No. 145). Released in winter; governor says "You have been here for twenty years." Fanshawe waits at prison gates, takes his money; says "Charlie"; reveals himself; sets off on a train to London.
2. Fanshawe's room near river; girl Moggs; Fanshawe reveals seven years in prison for forgery and fraud. Charles goes to Hammerstone Market; sees young Charles (Arnold? no—a boy) meeting new Barbara in wood; overhears new Barbara singing at Patton house; "Barbara, you have your mother's voice." Charles lies to boy.
3. Fanshawe introduces Charles to Murray Olivant (rich), who names him "Tinman." Fanshawe reports first Barbara died at sea (suicide note). Lucas Savell broken; business taken by Olivant. Olivant sends Tinman to Hammerstone Market; Barbara (new) meets him; ghost-like face at window.
4. Olivant comes; humiliates Barbara, insists she come down; Arnold confronts him ("Go and sit down!"); Tinman threatens Olivant ("I killed a man once"); Charles befriends new Barbara; Tinman stands watch on stairs.
5. Next day Tinman arranges with Arnold to rescue Barbara; Fanshawe spies. Olivant ambushes Tinman in his room, binds and gags him; Dawkins forges a note signed TINMAN, sending Barbara with Dawkins to London.
6. Tinman escapes by tearing towel; Savell sees Barbara's ghost on terrace; Barbara (first) reveals she is alive; Arnold vows to kill Olivant; Olivant tells Savell Barbara ran off with Arnold.
7. Barbara (first) explains her escape: stewardess, veil, name Barbara Avaline. Tinman at Trafalgar Square; Olivant returns; Dawkins sends letter demanding £500; Arnold waits outside Olivant's rooms.
8. Dawkins has Barbara (new) in Moggs's lodging; Tinman assists the enemy? Fanshawe overhears, Barbara is hidden. Olivant "Here is she!" hoax; Arnold ejected by constable.
9. Olivant plans faked voyage on the Eaglet; takes tickets; new clothes; secures rooms in Lincoln's Inn Fields. Fanshawe steals tickets; Charles buys sailor's knife.
10. Tinman finds Olivant already dead in Lincoln's Inn Fields rooms, stabbed; Charles flees; Fanshawe was the killer (confesses to Charles in rooms). Fanshawe sails on Eaglet with stolen tickets; ship wrecked; he dies.
11. Charles tells first Barbara that he killed Olivant (lie). First Barbara returns to Lucas. Lucas suffers stroke; Barbara (first) reunites; Lucas dies.
12. Charles, freed, returns to Hammerstone Market; new Barbara marries Arnold at the church; Charles hugs and is kissed by new Barbara. Charles and first Barbara (Charles and Barbara) marry; ending: she keeps his name.

## Key quotes
- "I have lived two lives."
- "Because I love you and trust you, I give you this, my dear, to read and then to burn."
- "I will reach you—God willing—before they kill you!"
- "Lucky at cards, unlucky in love."
- "The dead come alive."
- "Barbara, you have your mother's voice."
- "God is good; he has given my enemy into my hands at last!"
- Newspaper item: S.S. Eaglet lost off Ushant; sole survivor Henry Howard; passenger Mr. Murray Olivant.
